newsitem.title: USA: Ecuador's Bucaram seen pushing through reforms.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador's Bucaram seen pushing through reforms.

text.p: Ecuador's President Abdala Bucaram is likely to win the necessary backing from the country's lawmakers to enact structural reforms, Carlos Julio Emanuel, a member of Ecuador's monetary board, said on Thursday.
"I am fairly certain that he (Bucaram) is very capable politically to be able push his reforms through," Julio Emanuel said at a meeting sponsored by the Ecuadorean American Association.

"In the event that he doesn't get convertibility, I don't think he will turn back on the structural reforms," he said. Under the so-called convertibility plan, the country's currency would be pegged at four sucres to the dollar.

Julio Emanuel said there was support within the private sector for the structural reforms that have been announced -- tax reform, fiscal discipline, labor reform, social security reform and privatizations.
"The private sector holds the view that most Ecuadoreans share that these reforms are necessary for Ecuador to enter and compete effectively in a globalized economy," he said.
Still, Julio Emanuel said that Bucaram's political ability would play an important role as he tried to achieve a consensus in Congress on the proposals.
He said the threat of a general strike, scheduled to begin on February 5, will also test the president's political skills in getting the convertibility law implemented.

"It is clear to me that Bucaram is absolutely convinced that it is only a matter of time before Ecuador is under convertibility...so I don't foresee any possibility that he would change his mind on this matter," he said.
